j1.closes: E-18's run with a hash ring in place of slots

j2.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-10 and SC-03": as worded, the effective writer count is 12 to 22 for every design under Zipf 0.99, below F_w = 64 (the proposed value; E-18, simulated), because nothing splits the hottest partition. Restated it still fails: v4 places rows on members by ring hash alone, with no move that follows load, and E-18 shows hash-only placement passes max/mean 1.25 before 16 groups even with the app split (reasoned from E-18's fixN runs; the ring itself was not run). With `replicas` unset every member holds every row, so writes do not grow with servers at all.

j1.why: 1.3 line 'SC-10 and SC-03, every row': as worded every design reaches only 12 to 22 effective writers, below F_w = 64 (E-18). Restated, how an outside log spreads one resource over writers is theirs; on JetStream a stream is one group, and nothing here ran it.
j1.closes: a write-scaling run on the outside log, 1 to 4 servers

j2.why: Step 1: on JetStream a resource is one stream (E-44). Step 2: a stream is one Raft group with one leader, so every write of the resource goes through one writer. Step 3: more servers add no writer, and spreading a resource over several streams is a count chosen by hand, so it fails as worded and restated (1.3 line "SC-10 and SC-03"): 1 writer against 64.

j1.why: It shrinks only through the merge, a second protocol (37 rules with the split; the `shrink` bound holds, model-checked, crash-only). Lineage is kept for ever, a small lasting cost, and no load-cycle run exists.
j1.closes: phase 4: the sim of a daily load cycle over 7 days with the real mover and its grow and shrink thresholds

j2.why: Step 1: P `split` splits a group by size and load and has no merge; merge is PD's option. Step 2: in E-17b's model a resource shrinks only through the merge protocol: "a split alone never shrinks". Step 3: so groups made at a peak stay for good, which is a lasting cost from a past peak.

j1.why: 1.3 line 'SC-05 at 10 GB': fero's client would fold rows in Node at E-34's 10 s a GB, over the bar at 10 GB in one process. E-44 ran no sleep or wake, and whether the outside log comes back from a store alone is theirs to show, so it is open as worded and restated.
j1.closes: a sleep-and-wake run on the outside log, disks kept and lost

j2.why: Step 1: JetStream keeps a stream on its servers' file store (E-44) and has no object-store tier. Step 2: SC-05's test stops every server and wakes with servers that lost their disks. Step 3: then the streams are gone, so acknowledged writes are lost.

j1.why: Scoped replication (`replicas`) puts each partition on a few members, so a resource can pass one server's memory and disk. v4 has no cold rows and no object store, and no run at 3 x RAM exists.

j2.why: v4 keeps every row a server holds in memory and has no cold rows and no object-store tier. `replicas: N` spreads partitions over members, which covers the disk half only.

j1.why: The outside log keeps streams on disk, but fero's client folds every row it follows in Node memory. Nothing ran a data set at 3 x RAM.

j2.why: E-44's client folds the whole stream into memory, and one stream sits whole on each of its replicas, so a resource cannot pass one server's disk without a hand-chosen number of streams.

j1.why: Step 1: SC-07 asks clusters of 1 to 100 members to run in the sim. Step 2: BUY's members are an outside server's processes (nats-server). Step 3: fero's simulator cannot run their bytes, so no seed, sweep or replay of such a cluster can exist (E-44 says so in writing; SPACE 4.2).

j2.why: The sim cannot run nats-server's bytes (TEST-10), so only a real run of 100 servers could show this, and none was made.
j2.closes: A real 100-server JetStream run (not planned: BUY is the reference row).

j1.why: Step 1: in v4, adding or removing a server moves ring ownership of partitions. Step 2: STATUS.md pins a seed of v4's own simulator (scoped sweep A3, seed 6) where a forwarded write commits at the old owner and again at the new one across an ownership move. Step 3: SC-08(a) allows no doubled write during a scale change.

j2.why: v4's sim sweeps joins and leaves with monitors, but STATUS lists open cases: a held member that needs an operator, and a drain at one replica that loses rows when the new holder crashes. (b), (c) and (f) are not pinned at these bars.
j2.closes: Close STATUS's open membership cases, and pin (b), (c) and (f) in v4's scale tier.

j1.why: With a process per project (N `proc`) nothing is resident while a project sleeps, and it sends nothing (E-26 counts 0 groups). The 10 % clause is only reasoned: E-35 showed that tenants on one disk raise each other's p99 by 1.20 to 1.36 times even with a journal each, and no run gave each project its own volume.
j1.closes: the platform phase: two projects on the deploy target's volumes under E-35's load, and a box test with 1,000 sleeping projects

j2.why: N `proc`: each project has its own processes and its own volume, so a sleeping project holds nothing anywhere (E-26: 0 groups, 0 messages) and no log-tier process is shared. A busy project cannot reach another's journal or disk by construction (E-35 reasons this and did not test two machines). OPS-14's rules are judged under OPS-14.

j2.why: Its edge is native. E-08's Rust relay served 1,000 and 10,000 subscriber sockets from one core (13.4 and 11.9 million deliveries a second), so both counts hold. Idle-link memory in a native TLS stack was not measured (reasoned to be under Node's).

j1.why: 1.3 line 'SC-13's small': as worded, per-slot state costs about 85 B a touched slot, so an idle resource that touched 100 slots costs 8.8 KB against 2 KB (E-36, Node), and a denser form is still over once most slots are touched. Restated as 'few slots touched', a group per resource with dormant groups measured 1.4 KB and creates in 4.6 to 5.3 ms, but the cold-open tail is 5.4 to 7.6 ms against 5 ms, and drops and the create-and-drop sim were never run. It also depends on N_res.
j1.closes: phase 1 fixes the formats (run-length slot table, sparse per-slot state); phase 3 or 4: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second, with the cold-open and drop pins

j2.why: AMENDMENTS 1.3, line "SC-13's small": per-slot state costs about 85 B per touched slot in Node (E-36). With a run-length slot table, sparse per-slot state and dormant groups (A-15, A-16) an idle resource costs 1.4 KB at 10 touched slots and 8.8 KB at 100, against 2 KB; a create takes 4.6 to 5.3 ms against 10.7 ms, and a cold open 3.3 to 3.5 ms at the median but 5.4 to 7.6 ms at worst against 5 ms. As worded "small" is undefined; restated as "few slots touched" the memory clause holds, and it stays open because 1e5 resources (the proposed N_res) were not created and dropped through `fero()` and the drop clauses were not run.
j2.closes: Phase 2: the sim that creates and drops 1e5 resources at 100 a second through `fero()`, with a cold-open pin (G-16) and the drop clauses.
